question: Which of the following languages was granted classical status by the Government of India in 2005, following Tamil?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Sanskrit**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Sanskrit** was granted **classical language status** by the Government of India in **2005**, following Tamil, which was declared a classical language in **2004**.
 
• A language is granted classical status based on its **antiquity, rich literary tradition, and cultural heritage**.
 
• **Sanskrit** is one of the oldest languages in the world and is considered the **mother of many Indian languages**, forming the foundation of Indo-European linguistic traditions.
 
• The recognition of Sanskrit as a classical language highlights its role in preserving **ancient Indian texts, philosophy, and knowledge systems**, including the **Vedas, Upanishads, and epics like Mahabharata and Ramayana**.
